purpose: Configure rules, view status, manage the kernel audit subsystem
sections:
[{"title":"Status","code":"auditctl -s                    # Show current status (enabled, pid, backlog, etc.)
auditctl -l                    # List all loaded rules
auditctl -e 1                  # Enable auditing
auditctl -e 0                  # Disable auditing
auditctl -e 2                  # Make configuration immutable (until reboot)"},{"title":"Clear / load","code":"auditctl -D                    # Delete all rules
auditctl -R /etc/audit/audit.rules   # Load rules from a file"},{"title":"Buffer & failure mode","code":"auditctl -b 8192               # Set backlog buffer size
auditctl -f 1                  # Failure mode: 0=silent, 1=printk, 2=panic"},{"title":"File watches","code":"auditctl -w /etc/passwd -p wa -k identity
auditctl -w /etc/shadow -p rwa -k sensitive
auditctl -W /etc/passwd        # Remove a watch"},{"title":"Syscall rules","code":"auditctl -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S execve -k process_creation
auditctl -a always,exit -F arch=b64 -S open,openat -F exit=-EACCES -k access_denied
auditctl -d always,exit -F arch=b64 -S execve -k process_creation   # Delete a rule"},{"title":"Useful filters","code":"-F auid>=1000
-F auid!=unset
-F uid=0
-F euid!=uid
-F path=/usr/bin/sudo
-F exit=-EPERM
-F key=mykey"}]
notes: Permission flags for -p: r = read, w = write, x = execute, a = attribute change

purpose: Search and display events from the audit logs
sections:
[{"title":"By key","code":"ausearch -k identity
ausearch -k access_denied -i          # -i = interpret (human-readable)"},{"title":"By time","code":"ausearch -ts today
ausearch -ts recent                   # Last 10 minutes
ausearch -ts 10:00:00 -te 11:00:00
ausearch -ts 01/15/2025"},{"title":"By user / process","code":"ausearch -ua 1000                     # auid
ausearch -ui 0                        # uid
ausearch -ul root                     # login name
ausearch -p 12345                     # pid
ausearch -pp 1234                     # ppid"},{"title":"By syscall / success","code":"ausearch -sc execve
ausearch -sc open,openat
ausearch -sv yes                      # success=yes
ausearch -sv no                       # success=no"},{"title":"By file / executable","code":"ausearch -f /etc/passwd
ausearch -x /usr/bin/sudo"},{"title":"By message type","code":"ausearch -m SYSCALL
ausearch -m USER_AUTH,USER_LOGIN
ausearch -m AVC"},{"title":"By event ID","code":"ausearch -a 24287"},{"title":"Output formats","code":"ausearch -k identity -i               # Interpret
ausearch -k identity --raw            # Raw
ausearch -k identity -i -c cat        # Interpret + command name filter
ausearch -k identity --format csv
ausearch -k identity --format text"}]

purpose: Generate summary reports from the audit logs
sections:
[{"title":"Reports","code":"aureport                           # Summary report
aureport --summary                 # Overall summary
aureport --auth                    # Authentication report
aureport --login                   # Login report
aureport --file                    # File access report
aureport --executable              # Executable report
aureport --host                    # Host report
aureport --user                    # User report
aureport --terminal                # Terminal report
aureport --key                     # Key report
aureport --syscall                 # Syscall report
aureport --anomaly                 # Anomaly report
aureport --failed                  # Failed events only
aureport --success                 # Successful events only
aureport --start today
aureport --start this-week
aureport -i                        # Interpret numeric values"}]

[{"title":"Service management","code":"systemctl status auditd
systemctl start auditd
systemctl stop auditd
systemctl restart auditd           # Note: often requires service auditd restart
service auditd restart             # Preferred on many systems (preserves rules)"},{"title":"Signals","code":"kill -TERM $(pidof auditd)         # Clean stop
kill -HUP  $(pidof auditd)         # Reconfigure (reread auditd.conf)
kill -USR1 $(pidof auditd)         # Rotate logs
kill -USR2 $(pidof auditd)         # Resume logging after suspend"}]

augenrules --check"}]
